source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025) Sound and Complete Neurosymbolic Reasoning with LLM-Grounded Interpretations
finding: An LLM judge is placed inside a Belnap-style four-valued semantics. For each claim it gives a pair: could it verify, could it refute. Contradictions (both) stay local and do not explode the theory.
numbers: Tests on GPQA and SimpleQA claims with 6 models (3 flagship: Llama 4 Maverick, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet; 3 distilled). 2x400x18 = 14,400 calls.
quote: contradictions are localized rather than causing logical explosion
limits: Only the LLM-as-judge is tested, not full multi-step proofs. Factuality only.
agent_relevance: Direct template for S6: hold a claim as verified AND refuted without collapse.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025) Sound and Complete Neurosymbolic Reasoning with LLM-Grounded Interpretations (accuracy vs coverage)
finding: Bilateral (verify + refute) evaluation beats a single true/false judge on macro F1 when it may abstain on conflicted or unknown claims. It pays with coverage.
numbers: Macro F1 bilateral vs unilateral: GPQA flagship 0.699 vs 0.633, distilled 0.608 vs 0.559; SimpleQA flagship 0.736 vs 0.657, distilled 0.624 vs 0.570. Coverage 0.589/0.504 (GPQA), 0.584/0.499 (SimpleQA) vs 1.0. Mean F1 gain 0.062, coverage change -0.456 (p<0.01).
limits: F1 is computed only on non-abstained items, so the gain is selective classification, not better reasoning. Flagship beat distilled by 0.091 (GPQA) and 0.112 (SimpleQA) bilaterally.
agent_relevance: Two-sided check lets the agent mark 'conflicted' and hold back, trading coverage for precision.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025) Sound and Complete Neurosymbolic Reasoning with LLM-Grounded Interpretations (cost)
finding: Asking the model twice (verify, then refute) costs about double the time and tokens.
numbers: GPQA flagship: 36.7 s and 4,782 tokens bilateral vs 12.4 s and 2,213 tokens unilateral. SimpleQA flagship: 32.8 s and 4,164 tokens vs 12.3 s and 2,100.
limits: Bootstrap SEs only; single run per item.
agent_relevance: Use the two-sided check only on claims that matter at an impasse, not every step.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025) Sound and Complete Neurosymbolic Reasoning with LLM-Grounded Interpretations (glut vs gap rates)
finding: Models find both support and refutation (glut) more often than neither (gap). Rates differ strongly by model family.
numbers: Flagship GPQA: (t,t)=0.301, (t,f)=0.211, (f,t)=0.378, (f,f)=0.110. SimpleQA topic table: GPT family glut avg 59.0%, gap ~0.1%; Claude glut 19.6%, gap 30.4%; Llama glut 52.9%. Video games glut 63.6%, sports 47.3%, history 35.7%. Inconsistency more frequent than incompleteness (p<0.05).
limits: Glut counts depend on prompt wording. Models from 2024-25 only. The error value 'e' never occurred.
agent_relevance: Contradiction rate from one model is not a stable signal. Calibrate per model before using 'glut' as a trigger.

source: Allen, Chhikara, Ferguson, Ilievski, Groth (2025) Sound and Complete Neurosymbolic Reasoning with LLM-Grounded Interpretations (medication safety demo)
finding: A rule base with deliberately wrong rules (benzodiazepines non-addictive, NSAIDs cardiosafe) was forward-chained. The LLM judge flagged the contradictions and the theory stayed satisfiable.
numbers: 92 contradictions found, theory remained satisfiable. All 25 opioids gave gluts for Nonaddictive(X); 11 gluts for beta-blockers in asthma; 7 for fluoroquinolones in children. Reasoner under 10 ms; LLM calls over 99% of runtime.
limits: Worked example, one judge (GPT-4o), no accuracy metric against a human gold set.
agent_relevance: Shows a loop: derive, check with LLM, record gluts, keep deriving. Fits S6 impasse work.

source: Chan, Gaizauskas, Zhao (2025) RULEBREAKERS: Challenging LLMs at the Crossroads between Formal Logic and Human-like Reasoning
finding: Rule-correct answers (disjunctive syllogism, modus tollens) can be wrong when premises clash with world knowledge. Humans say nothing follows. LLMs apply the rule rigidly.
numbers: 7 LLMs. Chance paired accuracy 0.25. Only Llama-3-8B-Instruct exceeded 0.6. GPT-4o, Gemma-2-27b and Phi-3-mini scored near perfect on non-rulebreakers but worst on rulebreakers. GPT-4o scored 0.0022 on the MT categorical-entity subset.
limits: Dataset is country/city and type/instance pairs; ICML 2025. Paired accuracy needs both items right.
agent_relevance: This is the do-not-over-infer test. Logic-style scaffolds can hurt here.

source: Chan et al. (2025) RULEBREAKERS (confidence and prompt effects)
finding: Models are more confident in yes for valid cases than for rulebreakers, so they hold a latent signal that output tokens hide. Rewording and premise prefixes help but trade off.
numbers: Confidence for non-rulebreakers > rulebreakers for all models (p<0.0001). Prefix 'Suppose we are told... as a matter of fact' plus alternate phrasing gave up to +24.13 paired accuracy (gemma-2-27b-it, ending at 31.27); best final 69.12 (Llama-3-8B). Mistral-7B: +5.58 non-rulebreakers, -13.62 rulebreakers. Llama-8B with extra instructions: +10.51 rulebreakers, -18.21 non-rulebreakers.
limits: Gains on one side cost the other in most models.
agent_relevance: Prompt fixes shift the error, they do not remove it. Measure both sides.

source: Chan et al. (2025) RULEBREAKERS (logic-enhanced pipelines)
finding: Adding formal logic tools made gpt-3.5-turbo worse on rulebreakers. A logic fine-tune also over-applies rules.
numbers: LogicLM and SymbolicCoT raised non-rulebreaker accuracy but cut rulebreaker accuracy, so paired accuracy fell below baseline. CoT showed a similar but smaller trade-off. Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B better on non-rulebreakers, much worse on rulebreakers (Table 10).
limits: Exact Table 10 cells not extracted here; gpt-3.5-turbo is an old model.
agent_relevance: Classical solver scaffolds do not give paraconsistent behaviour. They can worsen explosion-like errors.

source: Li, Li, Chang, Wu (2025) Don't Take the Premise for Granted: PCBench
finding: Models rarely notice contradictory premises unless told to check. Direct contradictions are easier than ones needing deduction.
numbers: 15 LLMs, 1,200 base problems, 4 error types, 3 difficulty levels. Proactive critique rate: GPT-4o 11.0%, DeepSeek-V3 40.5%, o4-mini 4.0%. Assisted (told to check): GPT-4.1 73.2%, Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking 77.9%, o4-mini 74.2%. DeepSeek-V3 proactive rate 48% Normal to 29% Hard. Contradictory Premise Insert over 55% for DeepSeek-V3.
limits: Math word problem domain. Judge is o3-mini-high; human agreement kappa 0.7763 on the GPT-4.1 check.
agent_relevance: An explicit check-premises-for-conflict step is worth roughly +30 to +60 points over no prompt. Build it into S6.

source: Li et al. (2025) PCBench (overthinking)
finding: Flawed premises make reasoning models loop and write far more, rather than stop and flag the conflict.
numbers: Cost ratio flawed vs normal: o3-mini PPCCR 3.90, APCCR 3.11; DeepSeek-R1 PPCCR 2.71. Qwen3 8B to 235B non-thinking: APCR 59.9% to 70.0%, PPCR 20.6% to 24.7%. Qwen3-235B thinking: PPCR 35.3%, APCR 70.1%, 3,629 tokens.
limits: Reasoning ability did not track critique ability; some models seem to spot the flaw internally but not say it.
agent_relevance: Add a hard budget at impasse; otherwise a contradiction burns tokens on repeated retries.

source: Hou et al. (2024) WikiContradict: Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Knowledge Conflicts from Wikipedia
finding: With two contradicting passages, models usually answer from one and ignore the other. Telling them to attend to the conflict helps a lot, mainly for explicit conflicts.
numbers: 253 annotated instances (64% explicit, 36% implicit). Human-eval subset 48 instances. Llama-3-70b-instruct correct answers: 10.4% to 43.8% with a conflict-aware prompt; GPT-4 6.3% to 10.4%. Llama-3-70b explicit conflicts 13.3% to 60.0%, implicit 5.9% to 17.6%. Auto judge F-score 0.8.
limits: Small human-eval subset (48). GPT-4 showed stubborn reliance on internal knowledge. Annotator kappa 0.58 to 0.88 by prompt.
agent_relevance: Implicit contradictions need more than a prompt; add a derive-then-compare step.

source: Cattan et al. (2025) DRAGged into CONFLICTS: conflicting sources in search-augmented LLMs
finding: A taxonomy of conflict types (no conflict, complementary, freshness/misinformation, opinions) with a different right behaviour for each. Naming the conflict type before answering raises quality.
numbers: 458 instances. Conflict-type prediction accuracy: Gemma 3 27B 53.9, Qwen 2.5 72B 53.1, GPT-4o 59.2, Gemini 2.0 Flash 60.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash 65.3. Adherence to expected behaviour: Vanilla 59.4 to 68.3; Oracle +24 points on average; pipeline +9, taxonomy-aware +5.5. Conflicting opinions: 36.2 vanilla, 73.3 pipeline, 87.9 oracle (Gemini 2.5 Flash thinking).
limits: Judge is Gemini 2.5 Flash. Predicting the type is itself only about 65% accurate, so most of the oracle gain is not reached.
agent_relevance: Classify the contradiction (error, update, opinion) before choosing to repair, keep both, or report both.

source: MAGIC authors (2025) MAGIC: Multi-Hop and Graph-Based Benchmark for Inter-Context Conflicts in RAG
finding: Conflict detection across two contexts is harder when it needs several hops, and pinpointing where the conflict lies is harder still.
numbers: 1,080 examples. Averages: identification ID ECON 74.73, WikiContradict 69.93, MAGIC 64.54; localisation LOC 57.09, 55.74, 40.51. GPT-4o-mini best (ID 83.61, LOC 55.00 on MAGIC); Mixtral worst (37.92, 17.40); o1 68.06 and 49.72. Llama gave no answer in 47.4% of runs. Stepwise prompt beat naive prompt by up to 39.41%.
limits: Author names not recorded. Scores hand-computed by researchers. GPT-4o-mini also rendered the text.
agent_relevance: Detection is easier than localisation, and localisation is what a repair step needs.

source: Bienvenu, Bourgaux, Kozhemiachenko (2024) Queries With Exact Truth Values in Paraconsistent Description Logics (KR 2024)
finding: A non-LLM system: four-valued (T, F, Both, Neither) querying of inconsistent ontologies. Queries can ask for exactly true versus has contradictory evidence. Compared with repair-based semantics, the two approaches are incomparable.
numbers: Data complexity stays tractable for Horn DLs; for ALCHI-family, combined complexity is ExpTime-complete in several cases.
limits: Theory paper. No LLM and no empirical accuracy numbers.
agent_relevance: A model for answering what is known despite the conflict, with a cost bound.

source: Salla, Amancherla, Saravanan (2026) Quantifying Cross-Query Contradictions in Multi-Query LLM Reasoning
finding: An LLM agent loop that extracts commitments, checks them with a solver, and repairs the smallest conflicting set. This keeps a globally satisfiable belief state.
numbers: 390 instances, 4 domains. SetCons 0.56 (No-CoT) to 0.94 (SC K=20) for DeepSeek-R1. Ablation averages: no solver 0.52, check-only 0.84, repair without core 0.88, core-guided repair 0.91; revision cost 2.2 to 0.4; overhead 1.51x. gpt-oss-120b No-CoT 0.52, SC 0.92. Label kappa 0.82.
limits: ICLR 2026 workshop paper. Per-model check+repair SetCons cells were not readable in the extraction. Self-consistency (K=20) reached 0.88 to 0.94 without a solver.
agent_relevance: Closest published repair loop: detect, find the conflict core, retract the least, continue. Cheap relative to 20-sample voting.

source: Salla et al. (2026) cross-query contradictions (accuracy effects)
finding: Making answers jointly consistent did not come mainly from saying unknown more often. Accuracy did not fall.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1 accuracy: No-CoT 0.80, CoT 0.84, SC 0.86, Check+Repair 0.85. Deep-subset average: core-guided repair 0.81 vs no-solver 0.77.
limits: Same workshop-paper caveats; only 390 cases.
agent_relevance: Repair gives coherence at no accuracy cost.

source: Nguyen et al. (2026) BIS Reasoning 1.0: Belief-Inconsistent Syllogistic Reasoning
finding: When a valid argument ends in a conclusion that clashes with belief, models without explicit reasoning follow belief. Reasoning effort and prompt framing change this a lot.
numbers: 5,000 Japanese syllogisms. GPT-5-mini 99.72%, Qwen3-32B 99.58% (no thinking), GPT-4o 79.54%, GPT-4-turbo 59.48%, GPT-5-nano medium effort 98.84% vs minimum effort 69.22%, Claude-3-opus 7.18%, Claude-3-sonnet 20.34%. On 100 GPT-4o failures: CoT prompt fixed 87%, strict-logic prompt 76%.
limits: Japanese only. Syllogisms are not contradictory sets. Claude-3 models are deprecated.
agent_relevance: Belief-versus-logic conflict is a cousin of premise conflict. Reasoning budget matters.

source: Dhanda (2026) DeltaLogic: minimal premise edits reveal belief-revision failures
finding: Models that reason well on fixed premises still fail to revise when one premise changes. They keep the old answer (inertia).
numbers: 30-episode Qwen subset. Qwen3-1.7B initial 0.667, revised 0.467, inertia 0.600; Qwen3-4B initial 0.650, revised 0.450, inertia 0.600; Phi-4-mini initial 0.950, revised 0.850; Qwen3-0.6B near-universal abstention.
limits: Tiny sample, small models only, workshop paper.
agent_relevance: If S6 retracts a premise, test it: old conclusions may persist after the premise is dropped.

source: Priest (1979) The Logic of Paradox (LP)
finding: Three-valued logic with true, false, and both. Contradictions do not entail everything. In LP, disjunctive syllogism fails.
numbers: No numbers (formal logic).
limits: Not opened this session; from background knowledge.
agent_relevance: LP's failure of disjunctive syllogism is the formal cousin of what rulebreaker items probe.

source: Belnap (1977) A useful four-valued logic
finding: Four values (true, false, both, neither) for a machine reasoning over sources that may conflict or be silent.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened; background knowledge. Allen et al. use this as their semantics.
agent_relevance: The model for tracking support and refutation separately per claim.

source: da Costa (1974) On the theory of inconsistent formal systems
finding: Founding calculi C_n that tolerate contradiction while limiting what follows, using a well-behaved operator.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened; background knowledge.
agent_relevance: Idea: mark which claims are trusted as consistent, and allow classical inference only for those.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with symbolic solvers
finding: LLM translates to logic and a classical solver reasons. Classical solvers give no useful answer on inconsistent input.
numbers: Numbers not recorded.
limits: Not read this session. RULEBREAKERS found Logic-LM style pipelines hurt rulebreaker accuracy (see c08).
agent_relevance: A classical solver in the loop needs a consistency check or paraconsistent front end first.

source: Maluszynski and Szalas, 4QL four-valued query language, in IJCAI 2015 inquiry dialogue paper
finding: A rule language with true, false, inconsistent, unknown, used in inquiry and persuasion dialogue systems. An older working paraconsistent AI system.
numbers: Not read; only a search-result summary was seen.
limits: Search snippet only.
agent_relevance: Four-valued dialogue states could track agent debate: agreed, disputed, open.

source: Arieli and Avron (1996) four-valued approach for recovering consistent data from inconsistent assertions
finding: Four-valued semantics used to recover consistent information from an inconsistent assertion set.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Seen only as a mention in a search result (title and venue not verified).
agent_relevance: Background for a use-what-is-safely-derivable mode.

source: Wei et al. (2022) chain-of-thought and Wang et al. (2022) self-consistency, as baselines in the cross-query study
finding: Baselines in the cross-query paper: SC with K=20 gave SetCons 0.88 to 0.94 across five models versus 0.46 to 0.56 without CoT.
numbers: Figures come from Table 1 of the cross-query paper (see c15).
limits: Original papers not opened.
agent_relevance: Cheap voting is a strong baseline against any solver loop.

source: Search-result summaries only: AGM-Bench, ReviseQA, LogicVault, ECF-Bench, CRTBench
finding: Reported as 2025-26 benchmarks of belief revision and cross-query consistency. LogicVault reportedly cut cross-query contradictions by 78% across six LLMs using an SMT solver and unsat-core feedback. AGM-Bench reportedly finds models retain retracted information.
numbers: 78% reduction (LogicVault, per search snippet only).
limits: Abstract-level only, not read. Treat as leads.
agent_relevance: Follow up before relying on these numbers.

source: Gap statement: no LLM study found that tests explicit explosion or paraconsistent proof search directly
finding: Across 7 web searches, no paper measured whether an LLM derives arbitrary conclusions from a contradictory premise set. The closest tests are premise critique, knowledge conflict detection, and the Belnap-judge work.
numbers: arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned rate-limit errors (429), so discovery came from WebSearch only.
limits: A gap claim limited by the few searches available.
agent_relevance: The S6 design is mostly untested ground; run an in-house check.
